title: EconOps Continuous Savings Initiative: batching, KV cache, quantization playbook
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Program-level initiative to capture sustained per-token cost reductions across hosted and dedicated deployments by unifying recommendations and runbooks for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles. Will produce: (1) an operational playbook with safe rollout patterns, (2) a prioritized backlog of infra and runtime changes, (3) automated experiments and dashboards to quantify unit-economics impact and guardrails for latency/quality regressions.
okrs: OKR-1: Reduce average cost-per-1K-tokens for customer workloads by 22% across hosted API (measured over trailing 30 days)
OKR-2: Increase auto-batching hit rate by 35% for median request patterns without violating 95th percentile latency SLOs
OKR-3: Roll out conservative quantization profiles to 25% of Dedicated capacity with <1% quality regression on prod eval sets
milestones: 2025-11-15: Kickoff + cross-functional alignment (runtime, infra, console, PM, design)
2026-01-10: MVP playbook published (batching heuristics + KV cache config recommendations)
2026-02-20: Controlled quantization experiment live on dedicated pool A
2026-04-10: Evaluate rollouts and finalize production rollout plan
deliverables: Playbook: batching parameters, request sizing, and backpressure handling
KV cache guide: TTL, eviction policies, and prefix caching best practices
Quantization matrix: model family -> safe quant profiles with quality thresholds
Console features: per-route batching heatmap, estimated unit savings, rollout toggles
A/B experiment harness and dashboards to measure token-cost delta and quality regression
acceptance_criteria: Automated telemetry shows cost reduction >= 18% on pilot customers within 30d (relative to baseline)
No SLO violations attributable to playbook changes in pilot environments
Runbook published and signed off by runtime, infra, and security leads
Console surfaces estimated savings per route and a one-click canary rollout toggle
risks: Latency regressions when aggressive batching interacts with bursty workloads
Quality regressions from quantization on niche model families not covered by eval sets
Customer surprise if rollout toggles change behavior without clear per-route visibility
Dependencies on kernel-level optimizations (ENG-3387) may delay timelines
